name: Ukraine
genZNote: Ukraine is Europe's largest country by area entirely within Europe, historically called the 'breadbasket of Europe' for its vast fertile farmland — and since 2022 it's also become the defining test case in current-affairs exams for territorial sovereignty and international law.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: The largest country entirely within Europe by land area, bordered by Russia, Belarus, Poland, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania, and Moldova, with a Black Sea coastline.
Dominated by vast, extremely fertile black-soil ('chernozem') plains, historically earning it the nickname 'the breadbasket of Europe'.
The Dnipro River is the country's major waterway, running through the capital, Kyiv.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Ukrainian is the official language, a distinct East Slavic language with its own literary tradition, alongside a significant Russian-speaking population in parts of the country.
Predominantly Orthodox Christian, with religious institutions playing a significant role in national identity, particularly amid recent political shifts away from Russian church affiliation.
Rich folk-art traditions, including elaborately decorated Easter eggs (pysanky) and embroidered clothing (vyshyvanka), central to national cultural identity.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A semi-presidential republic with a directly elected President and a Prime Minister-led government, alongside a unicameral parliament (Verkhovna Rada).
Gained independence from the Soviet Union in 1991 following its dissolution, later undergoing major pro-democracy movements including the 2004 Orange Revolution and 2014 Euromaidan protests.
Since February 2022, has been under full-scale invasion by Russia, a war that has become a central focus of global diplomacy, sanctions regimes, and international humanitarian response.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: Not currently a member of the EU or NATO, though it formally applied for EU membership in 2022 and was granted EU candidate status the same year.
Has received extensive military, financial, and humanitarian support from the United States, European Union, and other Western allies since Russia's 2022 invasion.
The war has caused a major global grain and energy supply disruption, given Ukraine's and Russia's significant roles in global wheat and fertiliser exports.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Ukraine maintain diplomatic relations dating to 1992, with India importing sunflower oil and, historically, defence equipment components from Ukraine.
India evacuated thousands of its citizens, largely medical students, from Ukraine in 2022 through 'Operation Ganga' following the outbreak of war.
India has maintained a policy of neutrality regarding the Russia-Ukraine conflict, calling for dialogue and diplomacy while continuing trade and humanitarian assistance to Ukraine.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: Historically one of the world's largest exporters of wheat, corn, and sunflower oil, given its exceptionally fertile agricultural land.
Also historically significant in steel production and aerospace/defence manufacturing (a legacy of Soviet-era industrial infrastructure).
The economy has been severely disrupted by the ongoing war since 2022, with major reconstruction and international financial support needs.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Being one of the world's largest historical grain and sunflower oil exporters — 'the breadbasket of Europe'.
The ongoing war with Russia since February 2022, a central issue in contemporary global geopolitics.
The 2004 Orange Revolution and 2014 Euromaidan pro-democracy movements.
Rich folk-art traditions including pysanky (decorated eggs) and vyshyvanka embroidery.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Ukrainian Hryvnia (UAH).
Historically known as a major grain producer ('the breadbasket of Europe'), a top global exporter of wheat, corn, and sunflower oil.
Economy has been severely disrupted by Russia's full-scale invasion beginning in 2022.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Vast fertile steppe (chernozem/black-soil) region underpins its agricultural strength.
The Carpathian Mountains in the west and the Dnipro River are major geographic features.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Traces roots to Kievan Rus', a medieval East Slavic state.
Was part of the Russian Empire and later the Soviet Union; declared independence in 1991 following the USSR's dissolution.
Faced Russian annexation of Crimea in 2014 and a full-scale Russian invasion beginning in February 2022.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1991 independence following the collapse of the Soviet Union.
The 2014 'Euromaidan' revolution ousted a pro-Russian president and reoriented the country toward closer ties with the EU and the West.
Has been under martial law and active conflict since Russia's 2022 invasion.

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: State Space Agency of Ukraine has a long Soviet-era heritage in rocket engineering, including the Yuzhmash design bureau.
Developed significant domestic drone and defence technology, especially since 2022.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Football and gymnastics are traditional strengths.
Kyiv's Saint Sophia Cathedral is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Ukrainian folk traditions, including pysanka (decorated eggs) and vyshyvanka embroidery, are internationally recognised cultural symbols.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Member of the UN; a candidate for EU membership since 2022.
Not a NATO member, though seeking membership; has received significant military and humanitarian support from Western allies since 2022.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Ukraine is the largest country entirely within Europe, a semi-presidential republic and historic 'breadbasket of Europe' currently facing a full-scale Russian invasion since February 2022.
keyFacts: Semi-presidential republic; independent since the 1991 Soviet collapse.
Granted EU candidate status in 2022; not currently an EU or NATO member.
Historically one of the world's largest wheat and sunflower oil exporters.
commonConfusion: Ukraine has EU candidate status (granted 2022) but is NOT yet a full EU member, and remains outside NATO — these are distinct stages, not the same thing.

highYieldFacts: Ukraine: semi-presidential republic, independent since 1991, largest country entirely within Europe.
Historic 'breadbasket of Europe'; granted EU candidate status in 2022.
India-Ukraine: India ran 'Operation Ganga' (2022) to evacuate citizens; India maintains a neutral diplomatic stance on the war.
commonTraps: Assuming Ukraine is already an EU or NATO member — it holds only EU candidate status as of 2022.
Confusing the 2004 Orange Revolution with the 2014 Euromaidan protests — these are two distinct pro-democracy movements a decade apart.
mustRemember: Ukraine: 'breadbasket of Europe', semi-presidential republic, EU candidate since 2022, under Russian invasion since Feb 2022; India ran Operation Ganga evacuation.

sources.name: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India — India-Ukraine Relations and Operation Ganga
